brief.text:
THE JOB OF THIS SCREEN, AND WHAT CHANGED

Four jobs happen here — fix what is wrong, look one line up, read what the shelf is worth, receive and count — and the earlier console already ordered them well. What it still did was SAY things in figures and sentences that the owner then had to turn into a picture in their head. This pass draws the picture.

1. THE POSITION IS ONE STRIP, THREE INSTRUMENTS. Not five tiles of numbers: the shelf's value with its 30-day line; the whole shelf as one bar, coloured by state, whose segments ARE the filter; and every paced line sorted into days of cover, with your 14-day cover drawn through it. "7 below their floor" now shows seven of how many, without a word.

2. THE MAP IS THE SCREEN'S CENTRE. Every line placed by how long it lasts (right) and how much money is in it (up). The three zones under it are the three lanes: what to buy before you lose a sale, what is fine, and the money already spent that is not coming back. A dot, its lane card and the open line in the rail are the same product.

3. EVERY ROW CARRIES ITS OWN BAR. In the register, days of cover is a bar with the cover tick, value carries its share of the shelf, and the last 30 days sit beside each line as ten small bars. The eye finds the short bar before it reads a figure.

4. COLOUR ANSWERS ONE QUESTION EACH. Crimson is running out; amber is caution and dead money (hatched, so it reads without colour); ink is healthy; oxide is the one thing to do next — Receive a delivery. Direction of a movement is a glyph, never a colour: +60 and −60 are both ink.

5. THE PHONE ANSWERS "DO I HAVE IT, AND FOR HOW LONG?" — search first, the shelf bar in one card, each match with its cover bar, and the one accent in the thumb zone. Drawn at 390, not reflowed.

Every value is the app's own: the --ow-* tokens, the 11/12/13/14/19 ramp, Figtree + IBM Plex Mono, the .ow- console components already shipping. No new colour family, no new weight, no fourteenth button family.

carriers.text:
WHAT CARRIES THE INFORMATION

value of the shelf → a figure and a 30-day line
state of the shelf → one stacked bar; its segments filter the list
how long each line lasts → a bar to 60 days, with the cover tick; crimson when it ends inside the cover
money in a line → height on the map; a share bar under the value
what sold, lately → ten bars a row, thirty in an open line; receipts are the pale bars
sitting still → hatched, and a quiet-days count in place of cover
where the money is → bars by category, held-for-others hatched
how old the figures are → a 30-day cadence bar under the last count
a movement's size → a bar from a centre line, left for out, right for in
a movement's kind → a glyph: tag, tray, ruler, crossed circle, crate

Text is kept for the things only text can say: names, codes, causes, and the one sentence an open line reads out.
